segments.text: AT length, a good and gracious GOD hath brought me out of Ireland, where to the very last, the people heard the gospel gladly. In the northern parts, multitudes attended, and was I not bound for America, I would have stayed there much longer. People flock here as usual, and I am enabled to preach twice every day. In about ten days I purpose moving towards London in order to embark. How my wife is, I cannot tell, having not heard from her for some time; but I hope she will be resigned. This, this is the cry of my soul,――

Bind, Father, hand and foot thy son,
Nor leave thy work till all be done;
O never let me, LORD, go free,
Till all my heart’s resign’d to thee.
Then quickly to the altar lead,
And suffer me no more to plead;
No longer with the old |ADAM| bear,
Lead on, dear LORD, consume him there.

Surely I shall be taken at my word. May JESUS support me in a trying hour! I still beg a continued interest in your prayers,――and hoping this will find you with a thriving soul in a healthy body, I subscribe my self, honoured Sir,
Your most obliged, affectionate, though unworthy younger brother, in the glorious Gospel, G. W.
